A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, central theory, and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original simulations, trajectory-identifiability statistics, and reconstruction experiments with SINDy and Neural ODEs.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain. Appendix D.5 adds controlled reconstruction experiments, and Appendix C reports structural examination of gene regulatory networks.

M1.justification: The linear-basis SINDy and sparsity-regularized linear Neural ODE estimators retain their architectures, objectives, optimization, and selection procedures. The new theoretical result and experiments do not introduce an estimator or change the existing procedures.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds a limited structural examination of the E. coli and S. cerevisiae DREAM5 networks; v1 used gene-network statistics principally as motivation. The synthetic linear-ODE tasks and alternative sparsity ensembles remain. The additional plant-network statistics are contextual summaries, not new trajectory-fitting benchmarks.

E2.justification: SINDy and Neural ODEs remain the evaluated estimation methods. The added sensitivity experiments reuse these methods, with the observation-window experiment reporting Neural ODE results only; no comparator is added to or removed from an existing comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix D.5 introduces controlled evaluation designs using 10 matrices per dimension/sparsity configuration, initial-condition distances of 0.1, 0.5, and 1, and observation windows [0, 0.2], [0, 0.5], and [0, 1]. It evaluates matrix MSE alongside Hamming distance. Existing experimental settings remain; the main-text normalization correction from n to n squared agrees with v1's appendix formula and does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.5 directly tests whether proximity to an invariant subspace and shorter observation windows impair reconstruction, substantially extending the empirical examination of Lemma 4. Appendix C adds network case studies. The earlier regularization, trajectory-metric, and alternative-matrix analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The existing one-sided Welch tests and box-plot reporting remain unchanged. The new experiments also use box plots, without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure, significance test, or training-seed/repeated-run disclosure.

E6.justification: New Figures 10–11 report reconstruction-error distributions across initial-condition distances and observation windows, generally supporting worse recovery near invariant subspaces and with shorter observations. Appendix C adds zero-column findings for E. coli and S. cerevisiae. The original result figures are retained, including v1 Figures 10–14 as v3 Figures 12–16; these additions are not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: New Lemma 5 and its proof extend positive unidentifiability bounds beyond independent Bernoulli masks to general structured sparsity distributions satisfying a column-support condition. This materially broadens the theoretical scope. Definition 1 also corrects the missing requirement that the alternative matrix B differ from A.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraph, and conclusion retain the central claims: sparsity permits positive-probability unidentifiability, near-unidentifiability obstructs practical recovery, and estimator biases do not generally overcome these difficulties. The additions principally extend support for these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A substantially expands the interpretation of ideal observation assumptions and the limits of real-world applicability. Section 5.3 explains SINDy's low-dimensional behavior through thresholding, while Appendix C qualifies the reliability of gene-network ground truth. Appendix C also introduces an overly broad assertion of unidentifiability even for identifiable systems, creating tension with the paper's conditional identifiability results.

D1.justification: v3 adds a reproducibility statement with a link described as public source code and identifies the specific DREAM5 network file examined. Existing software, solver, optimizer, and regularization details remain. The new experiment description still ambiguously says four initial conditions while listing three distance values.

R1.justification: v3 adds Marbach et al. (2012) for the gene-network examples and Wang et al. (2024a) on hidden confounders. The broader related-work discussion and central positioning relative to Stanhope et al. and Qiu et al. remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative are retained, with localized rewrites and terminology corrections. v3 expands the appendix organization to separate assumptions, proofs, gene-network discussion, and experiments, and adds reproducibility and LLM-use statements.

P2.justification: v3 adds two sensitivity figures and a gene-network table while retaining the original plots. Existing figures and the software table are renumbered or repositioned. The ICLR format changes title styling, headers, typography, and float placement without substantially redesigning the retained displays.

improvement.justification: Lemma 5 broadens the theoretical support, and Appendix D.5 directly tests practical consequences that v1 supported less directly. The new code pointer also improves reproducibility documentation. These gains are limited by new interpretive errors: Appendix C describes sparsities as below thresholds although Table 1 shows them above, and its blanket data-only unidentifiability assertion conflicts with the conditional framework of Theorem 2.
